findings.title: G21.cc5.prefix-exactly-at-prehandshake pins an RF-2 refusal expectation on N=65536, which the operative preHandshake clause the subject itself quotes classifies as an accepted frame, not a refusal.
findings.measurement: The fixture bytes are 00 01 00 00, which decode as 4-byte big-endian unsigned N = 65536. The subject's own controlFrameEncoding.preHandshakeBoundQuoted carries the operative clause character-exact: 'Until helloAck is accepted, N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0 is refusal family RF-2, detected from the prefix alone; the receiver must refuse without buffering the body.' I evaluated that predicate against the fixture: 65536 > 65536 is false and 65536 == 0 is false, so the RF-2 predicate is FALSE for this payload. The same predicate is TRUE for the v7 sibling 65537 and TRUE for this corpus's own far-over member 16777216, both of which I decoded and evaluated the same way. Against that, members[0].expected reads 'RF-2 typed refusal from the prefix alone. No body is read.' and members[0].mutation reads 'Occupancy EV-5 exactByteIntent: oversize refused from the prefix without buffering the body. No body is authored because the receiver must refuse from the prefix alone.' Occupancy v4 retainedEvidence EV-5 exactByteIntent says 'CC-5 oversize is refused from the prefix without buffering the body' - it governs oversize, and 65536 is not oversize under the quoted clause; it is the last accepted value.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The artifact resolves a live contradiction inside already-closed law and states the resolution as a pinned fact, without warrant and without naming the contradiction. The closed CC-5 intent lists 'prefix exactly at, one over, and far over the operative bound' and then says 'Each is RF-2 typed'; the operative preHandshake bounds clause makes only N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0 RF-2. Those two clauses disagree about the boundary value, and the postHandshake clause agrees with the bounds reading, not the intent reading ('A frame exceeding the negotiated bound is RF-2' - exceeding, not reaching). The subject quotes all three clauses side by side in controlFrameEncoding and reconciles none of them; it silently adopts the intent reading in the one field where the choice becomes an observable pass property. It also imports EV-5's oversize sentence to justify a payload that is not oversize, so the justification chain is broken under either reading. There is a second, byte-level consequence: if the boundary value is admitted, as the operative clause requires, then a 4-byte file declaring a 65536-byte body and supplying none is an EOF-during-body case, which belongs to CC-4 ('EOF at every state') and to the CC-5 'truncated bodies' injection this very corpus lists at whatIsNotAuthored[8] as not authored. So the fixture is either a refusal case the contract does not mandate or a truncated-body case mislabelled as an oversize-prefix case, and the artifact does not say which.
findings.whyMustFix: Three grounds. First, the G21 lineage has twice recorded the opposite partition in accepted independent reviews of this same corpus family, and recorded it as correct: the g21-fixture-corpus.v7 review states 'N=65536 is NOT refused by the closed clause (refusal requires N greater than 65536), so a fixture at 65536 would be a pass case, not a CC-5 refusal case. The subject leaves "CC-5 prefix exactly at the operative bound" explicitly unauthored in whatIsNotAuthored. This is the correct partition.' Both g21-fixture-corpus.v7 and g21-fixture-corpus.v8, the two recorded corpora, carry that case at whatIsNotAuthored index 7 as unauthored. This corpus reverses a recorded partition without arguing against it. Second, the trap was named in advance and the remedy was specified. The g21-fixture-corpus.v5 review recorded observation G21FXV5-O3: 'A trap for the successor, not a defect here. ... At the pre-handshake bound, N equal to 65536 is therefore an acceptance case rather than a refusal. This corpus authors neither, leaving the case at whatIsNotAuthored[7], so no wrong expectation is pinned. A successor authoring index 7 must resolve what the pass property is before assigning it a refusal expectation, and that resolution belongs to the closed contract's owner, not to a fixture-authoring cycle.' This corpus authored index 7 and assigned it a refusal expectation without that resolution. Third, the resolution the subject makes is exactly the class of act D-293 Decision 8 does not delegate: Decision 8 grants fixture authoring under the agreed semantic and dependency constraints, not authority to settle a boundary semantic that the closed contract states two ways. Deciding whether the boundary value is admitted or refused is an amendment to control-protocol-contract.v2's refusal typing and belongs to that contract's owner. A pinned wrong expectation is worse than an unauthored case, because DR-G21 execution would later measure a conformant receiver as failing.
findings.remedy: Either withdraw members[0] and restore 'CC-5 prefix exactly at the operative bound' to whatIsNotAuthored and to remainderAfterThisCorpus, leaving the contract owner to resolve the tension; or keep the bytes and stop asserting the outcome - state the tension explicitly, quote both the CC-5 intent sentence and the preHandshake predicate, record that the expected outcome for N equal to 65536 is UNRESOLVED between them, and route the resolution to the owner of control-protocol-contract.v2 as named later work. What the artifact must not do is print 'RF-2 typed refusal from the prefix alone' and 'oversize' for a value its own quoted predicate does not refuse.

findings.title: The remainder inventory deletes the whole of 'prefix exactly at' and 'prefix far over' after authoring only their preHandshake halves, so the postHandshake halves of both cases disappear from the record.
findings.location: remainderAfterThisCorpus; whatIsNotAuthored (indices 7 and 8 of the recorded v7/v8 inventory, absent here)
findings.measurement: g21-leftover-join.v13 obligations[3].remainingNotAuthored.remainingCc5Injections holds ten entries, of which two are unqualified as to handshake phase: 'CC-5 prefix exactly at the operative bound' and 'CC-5 prefix far over the operative bound'. A third, 'CC-5 prefix one over the postHandshake bound', is phase-qualified. The recorded corpora g21-fixture-corpus.v7 and g21-fixture-corpus.v8 both carry the two unqualified entries verbatim in whatIsNotAuthored at indices 7 and 8. This subject authors two members whose ids, paths and mutation text are all explicitly preHandshake - G21.cc5.prefix-exactly-at-prehandshake and G21.cc5.prefix-far-over-prehandshake - and then removes both unqualified entries entirely: whatIsNotAuthored no longer contains either, and remainderAfterThisCorpus enumerates the survivors as 'truncated bodies, invalid UTF-8, duplicate members, unknown members, floats, negative integers, over-uint53 integers, and prefix one over the postHandshake bound' - eight entries, ten minus two. Against that, the subject's own cc5IntentQuoted carries the closed intent's parenthesis character-exact: 'prefix exactly at, one over, and far over the operative bound (pre- and post-handshake bounds separately)'.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The parenthesis the subject quotes directs that all three prefix positions be exercised against the pre- and post-handshake bounds separately. Authoring the preHandshake half of a folded entry therefore discharges half of it. Striking the entry wholesale records the postHandshake half as discharged when no bytes for it exist. After this corpus, 'prefix exactly at the postHandshake bound' and 'prefix far over the postHandshake bound' are named in no live clause of the subject: not in whatIsNotAuthored, not in remainderAfterThisCorpus, not in proposedLaterWork. They are silently gone. The asymmetry is visible inside the subject's own list: it keeps 'prefix one over the postHandshake bound' as a distinct survivor precisely because its preHandshake sibling was authored at v7, which is the same bookkeeping this corpus declines to perform for the two entries it acts on.
findings.whyMustFix: The split was specified in advance by an accepted review of this corpus family. g21-fixture-corpus.v5 review observation G21FXV5-O2 records: 'The remainder inventory is asymmetric in granularity. Index 16 separates the post-handshake bound explicitly, because the pre-handshake sibling is authored here, while indices 7 and 8 ("prefix exactly at the operative bound", "prefix far over the operative bound") keep both bound contexts folded into one entry each, although the closed CC-5 intent separates pre- and post-handshake bounds for all three prefix cases. Nothing is misclassified and no authoring claim is affected in either direction, since all of these entries are unauthored. A successor that authors any of them will need to split entries 7 and 8.' This subject is that successor, it authored both, and it did not split either. Separately, this is a remainder measurement made in the one place whose purpose is to bound what stays owed on OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING, and the G21 lineage treats an unwarranted remainder measurement as MUST-FIX: the anti-lockstep-hostile-goldens.v1 review carried CLAUDE-ALHG-V1-M-1 as MUST-FIX for stating a CC-5 remainder figure no governing byte carried, on the ground that 'a later G21 remasurement citing this artifact would inherit a number the G21 lineage deliberately never recorded'. The same inheritance risk applies with more force here, because the artifact does not merely miscount the remainder, it removes two closed-intent cases from it. The next leftover-join remasurement re-pinning remainingNotAuthored from this artifact would drop them.
findings.remedy: Split the two folded entries instead of deleting them. Retain 'CC-5 prefix exactly at the postHandshake bound' and 'CC-5 prefix far over the postHandshake bound' in whatIsNotAuthored and in remainderAfterThisCorpus alongside the already-retained 'CC-5 prefix one over the postHandshake bound', and state in remainderAfterThisCorpus that only the preHandshake halves of the two join entries are authored here. If the exactly-at member is withdrawn under CLAUDE-G21FXV9-M-1, its preHandshake half returns to the remainder as well.

findings.title: The far-over payload is a chosen value presented without acknowledging that 'far over' selects no unique integer, and the value chosen is byte-identical to the future 'exactly at the postHandshake ceiling' case with the opposite expectation.
findings.measurement: members[1] encodes N = 16777216, taken from $.transportAndFraming.framing.bounds.postHandshake, whose text is 'the ceiling either side may offer or accept is 16777216'. That integer is genuinely quoted, and the subject is candid that it is quoted rather than invented; I confirmed it live in the contract and confirmed 16777216 > 65536, so the RF-2 predicate is satisfied and this member's expected outcome, unlike members[0]'s, is correct. What the subject does not state is that the closed intent's phrase 'far over the operative bound' picks out an unbounded family of lawful payloads, of which 16777216 is one selection among many, whereas its authored sibling and the recorded v7 member are arithmetically determined - the v4, v5, v6 and v7 reviews all rest on that determinacy, e.g. 'One over the pre-handshake bound with the bound quoted as 65536 admits exactly one value, 65537.' The chosen value is also exactly the postHandshake ceiling, so the same four bytes 01 00 00 00 are 'far over' before helloAck and 'exactly at the ceiling' after it.
findings.whyItIsWrong: Non-unique selection is a ground that has already landed against this corpus family: the g21-fixture-corpus.v4 review records that 'the second landed v3 attack was that closed framing does not uniquely select "null" from the many legal non-object JSON texts'. Borrowing a quoted constant is the right instinct and avoids inventing a number, but it does not make the selection determined, and the artifact presents the payload as though quotation settled the choice. The ceiling collision then creates a concrete authoring hazard for the successor that CLAUDE-G21FXV9-M-2 shows is still owed: a later fixture for 'prefix exactly at the postHandshake bound' at the ceiling would have byte-identical content to this file under an opposite expectation, and the two would be distinguishable only by directory and filename, not by bytes.
findings.whyNotMustFix: The member's expected outcome is correct on the operative clause, the integer is genuinely quoted rather than invented, and no false refusal is pinned. The defect is that the artifact does not say the selection is a choice, and does not record the collision it creates for a case that remains owed. That is a completeness and honesty gap in a current-standing clause rather than a wrong pin.
findings.remedy: State in members[1].mutation that 'far over the operative bound' admits many lawful payloads and that 16777216 is selected as the contract's own recorded ceiling to avoid inventing a constant, and record explicitly that this payload coincides with the postHandshake ceiling so a later 'exactly at the postHandshake bound' fixture must not reuse these bytes.

summaryForCoordinator: REJECT at 2 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Custody and mechanics are clean: the subject is unmoved at 0289fd23... mode 0444 at both ends, all 21 recordedInputs digests recompute, both fixtures are 4-byte prefix-only files at 0444 in the flat v7 shape, HEAD never left 7a1b1b76, file 08 and COORD reproduce at their dispatch digests, required-now is 28, the DR-G21 row token is OPEN, platforms are ORDERED-EQUAL across G10 v2 and G23 v2 with Windows untouched, all four contract quotations are character-exact, no bare version token collides with 9, and no forbidden closure, SATISFY, theft or invention occurs anywhere in the document. The corpus fails on the merits of one of its two payloads. G21.cc5.prefix-exactly-at-prehandshake encodes N = 65536 and pins 'RF-2 typed refusal from the prefix alone' on it, but the preHandshake predicate the subject itself quotes refuses only N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0, and 65536 satisfies neither disjunct; the subject also imports EV-5's 'oversize' sentence to justify a payload that is not oversize. Both recorded predecessors leave this exact case unauthored, and two accepted reviews of this corpus family recorded the opposite partition as correct, the g21-fixture-corpus.v5 review naming it in advance as a trap and specifying that the resolution belongs to the closed contract's owner rather than to a fixture-authoring cycle.
